slot.archetype: volume from density then PV = nRT
slot.brief: From gas density at given T and P, compute molar mass or volume via the ideal gas equation.

stem: The density of an ideal gas is $2.0\ \text{g L}^{-1}$ at $300\ \text{K}$ and $1.64\ \text{atm}$. What is the volume occupied by $15\ \text{g}$ of this gas at $400\ \text{K}$ and $0.82\ \text{atm}$? (Given: $R = 0.082\ \text{L atm K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$)
working:
Step 1: Determine the molar mass ($M$) of the gas using the density form of the ideal gas equation:
$$d = \dfrac{PM}{RT} \implies M = \dfrac{dRT}{P}$$
$$M = \dfrac{2.0\ \text{g L}^{-1} \times 0.082\ \text{L atm K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1} \times 300\ \text{K}}{1.64\ \text{atm}} = \dfrac{49.2}{1.64} = 30\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$$

Step 2: Calculate the number of moles ($n$) in $15\ \text{g}$ of the gas:
$$n = \dfrac{m}{M} = \dfrac{15\ \text{g}}{30\ \text{g mol}^{-1}} = 0.5\ \text{mol}$$

Step 3: Calculate the volume occupied by this amount of gas at $T = 400\ \text{K}$ and $P = 0.82\ \text{atm}$:
$$V = \dfrac{nRT}{P} = \dfrac{0.5\ \text{mol} \times 0.082\ \text{L atm K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1} \times 400\ \text{K}}{0.82\ \text{atm}} = \dfrac{16.4}{0.82} = 20\ \text{L}$$

Alternatively, find the initial volume $V_1 = \dfrac{m}{d_1} = \dfrac{15\ \text{g}}{2.0\ \text{g L}^{-1}} = 7.5\ \text{L}$, then apply the combined gas law:
$$V_2 = V_1 \left(\dfrac{P_1}{P_2}\right)\left(\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}\right) = 7.5 \times \left(\dfrac{1.64}{0.82}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{400}{300}\right) = 7.5 \times 2 \times \dfrac{4}{3} = 20\ \text{L}.$$

Independent check: M = ρRT/P = 2.0×0.082×300/1.64 = 30 g/mol. n = 15/30 = 0.5 mol. V = nRT/P = 0.5×0.082×400/0.82 = 20 L.
